## Solution

We want to maximize
$$P = \left(\int_0^1 f(x)^{1/3}\,dx\right)\left(\int_0^1 f(x)^{1/5}\,dx\right)\left(\int_0^1 f(x)^{1/7}\,dx\right)$$
subject to $f:[0,1]\to(0,\infty)$ continuous with $\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = 1$.

**Key observation.** For any $0 < \alpha < 1$, the function $\varphi_\alpha(t) = t^\alpha$ is **concave** on $(0,\infty)$ (since $\varphi_\alpha''(t) = \alpha(\alpha-1)t^{\alpha-2} < 0$).

**Applying Jensen's inequality.** With the uniform probability measure on $[0,1]$ and the concave function $\varphi_\alpha$:
$$\int_0^1 f(x)^\alpha\,dx \;\leq\; \varphi_\alpha\!\left(\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx\right) = \left(\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx\right)^\alpha = 1^\alpha = 1.$$

Applying this with $\alpha = 1/3,\,1/5,\,1/7$:
$$\int_0^1 f^{1/3} \leq 1, \qquad \int_0^1 f^{1/5} \leq 1, \qquad \int_0^1 f^{1/7} \leq 1.$$

Since $f > 0$, each integral is strictly positive, so the product satisfies
$$P \;\leq\; 1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1.$$

**Equality is attained.** Take the constant function $f(x) \equiv 1$. It is continuous, strictly positive, and $\int_0^1 1\,dx = 1$. Each integral equals $\int_0^1 1\,dx = 1$, so
$$P = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1.$$

(Equality in Jensen for a strictly concave function holds iff $f$ is constant a.e.; here $f\equiv 1$ is the unique maximizer up to the constraint.)

**Conclusion.** The maximum possible value is
$$\boxed{1}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
